items.title: NASA Science
items.summary: Did this meteor come from that comet? Probably not. Although many meteors do originate from comets, there are thousands of comets that have visited the inner Solar System recently, and matching meteors to them can be tricky. And to be clear, the pictured comet is far behind the streaking meteor. Comet C/2025 R3 (PanSTARRS) was captured from Hautacam, France in April when the giant space iceberg sported impressive ion (blue) and dust tails. Sand-sized rocky debris that enters Earth’s atmosphere typically appears as meteors, while the colorful foreground streak here may indicate a complicated composition. This month three notable meteor showers will reach their peaks.

items.title: Duration and barriers of physical education teaching in primary schools in 6 French departments
items.summary: by Eric Hermand, Serge Durali, Hugues Rolan, Laurence Munoz, Thierry Pezé, Valentin Smee Purpose Regular physical activity plays an important role in preventing sedentary lifestyles and reducing the risk of chronic diseases. In French primary schools, Physical Education (PE) represents the main compulsory opportunity for structured physical activity during school hours. This study aimed to assess self-reported weekly PE duration among primary school teachers in six French departments and to identify teacher- and school-related factors associated with PE duration, as well as the main obstacles to PE delivery reported by teachers. Methods Between March 2021 and June 2024, as the survey implementation in the different areas took place, an anonymous online questionnaire was sent to primary school teachers in six French departments about the time spent teaching PE and their professional habits in this subject.
items.author: Eric Hermand, Serge Durali, Hugues Rolan et al.

items.title: State-aware adaptive multimodal fusion for ultra-short-term solar irradiance forecasting using sky cloud images
items.summary: by Houhang Zhao, Aiyi Song, Yu Jin, Haoxiang Yu As renewable energy penetration continues to increase, accurate ultra-short-term solar irradiance forecasting is essential for improving energy utilization and supporting power system operation. However, irradiance variations are jointly influenced by historical trends and rapid cloud changes, making traditional single-modal methods insufficient for capturing complex dynamics under varying weather conditions. This paper proposes a multimodal solar irradiance forecasting framework based on the collaborative representation of sky cloud images and numerical sequences. The framework introduces a heterogeneous modal state encoding mechanism and a state-aware adaptive selective attention fusion mechanism to enhance interactions between visual weather information and historical physical patterns.

items.title: Spreading depolarization drives distant connectivity changes in the focally injured cortex
items.summary: by Daria A. Lachinova, Maria P. Smirnova, Ilya V. Sysoev, Lyudmila V. Vinogradova Cortical spreading depolarization (SD), a slow-propagating wave of transient cellular depolarization, reliably occurs after acute brain injury but usually remains undetected. Focal brain injury is known to produce a network-level dysfunction that changes the strength and direction of connectivity far beyond lesion site (connectional diaschisis) that can underlie post-injury neurological dysfunction. We suggested that injury-induced SD could contribute to connectional diaschisis and studied the effects of SD on functional and effective connectivity in neural networks supporting cognitive and sensory functions. Electrographic recordings of cortical activity were obtained in freely behaving rats immediately after focal micro-injury of the frontal cortex.
items.author: Daria A. Lachinova, Maria P. Smirnova, Ilya V. Sysoev et al.

items.title: Pain, sensory acceptability, and treatment compliance following cryotherapy and topical anesthetics in children: A randomized clinical trial
items.summary: by Emine Zehra Aydın Çetin, Bilal Özmen This randomized clinical trial aimed to compare the effects of cryotherapy, anesthetic spray, and gel on pain, anxiety, physiological responses, taste acceptability, and treatment compliance in children aged 7–10 years undergoing their first dental treatment. 100 healthy children were randomly allocated into four groups: 10% lidocaine spray, 20% benzocaine gel, cryotherapy with distilled water cooled to +4 °C, and lidocaine spray cooled to +4 °C. Following topical application, buccal infiltration anesthesia was administered. Anxiety, pain, and physiological responses were assessed using the Modified Dental Anxiety Scale and Facial Image Scale, Wong-Baker FACES Pain Rating Scale, and pulse-oximeter.
items.author: Emine Zehra Aydın Çetin, Bilal Özmen

items.title: Yield determinants in rice under organic and conventional production systems: Implications for selection strategies
items.summary: by Sushmitharaj Dhanalakshmi Veeraraj, Karthika Rajendran The persistent yield gap remains a major challenge in organic agriculture despite its increasing importance for sustainable food production. The present study compared the performance of 80 diverse rice genotypes (62 landraces and 18 modern varieties) under two contrasting production systems (organic and conventional). The experiment was conducted during the Kharif seasons of 2023 and 2024 using an alpha lattice design (8 × 10) with three replications. Agro-morphological and yield-related traits were analysed through pooled mixed-model analysis of variance (ANOVA), genetic variability parameters, correlation and path coefficient analyses, as well as principal component analysis (PCA).
items.author: Sushmitharaj Dhanalakshmi Veeraraj, Karthika Rajendran

items.title: Short-video content perceptions, intention, and self-reported behavior in special forces-style tourism: Evidence from Chinese generation Z university students
items.summary: by Hongjing Mo, Min Wei, Jingyu Liu Special Forces-style tourism is an emerging high-intensity, low-cost travel phenomenon among young people in China. Drawing on a modified Theory of Planned Behavior, this study analyzes survey data from 526 Chinese Generation Z university students using PLS-SEM and fsQCA. Perceived content appeal, perceived content trustworthiness, attitude, and perceived behavioral control are positively associated with intention, which is positively associated with self-reported behavior; short-video platform usage intensity strengthens this association. fsQCA identifies two configurations for high and eight for low self-reported behavior. Intention, perceived content trustworthiness, perceived behavioral control, and platform usage intensity form the common core of both high-outcome configurations, while low perceived content trustworthiness appears in six low-outcome configurations.
items.author: Hongjing Mo, Min Wei, Jingyu Liu

items.title: A Baltic Sea microbiome-derived Type III polyketide synthase produces host-protective alkylresorcinols in E. coli
items.summary: by Susana López-Gutiérrez, Laura A. Espinosa-Barrera, Arianna Soto-Hernández, Holber Zuleta-Prada, Celia Bustos-Brito, César S. Cardona-Félix, José Utrilla, Beatriz Velazquez-Cruz, Yair Cárdenas-Conejo, Jesus Alfredo Araujo-León, Victor Aguilar-Hernández, Juan A. Osuna-Castro, Baldomero Esquivel, Hugo Serrano-Posada, Sara Centeno-Leija Marine microorganisms are a prolific source of novel polyketide synthases (PKSs) that generate structurally diverse and functional polyketides. Here, we identify a novel type III PKS, ArsMB, from Pontimonas sp. via metagenomic mining of a Baltic Sea microbiome. Heterologous expression of ars MB synthetic gene in an Escherichia coli host that lacks a native type III PKS, combined with a two-step strategy to boost acyl-CoA precursor availability in a glucose-mineral medium, enabled the in vivo synthesis of two cell-associated alkylresorcinols, identified by GC-MS as 5-pentadecyl-1,3-benzenediol (ars1) and 5-tridecyl-1,3-benzenediol (ars2).
items.author: Susana López-Gutiérrez, Laura A. Espinosa-Barrera, Arianna Soto-Hernández et al.

items.title: Sex difference in survival benefits of immune checkpoint inhibitors in advanced non-small cell lung cancer: A meta-analysis
items.summary: by Tingting Liu, Dandan Song, Jun Chen, Jiacheng Yao, Jiehao Liao, Jun Dang Background Whether sex influences the survival benefit of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains uncertain. Methods We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Scopus up to April 1, 2026, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing ICIs with chemotherapy and reporting overall survival (OS) or progression-free survival (PFS) stratified by sex. A random-effects model was used for meta-analysis. Results Sixty-three publications (reporting 42 phase 3 RCTs) involving 25,827 patients (18,772 male; 7,055 female) were included. Compared with chemotherapy, ICIs significantly improved both OS and PFS in males (OS: HR 0.74 [95% CI 0.71–0.78]; PFS: HR 0.59 [95% CI 0.54–0.64]) and females (OS: HR 0.83 [95% CI 0.77–0.90]; PFS: HR 0.76 [95% CI 0.66–0.86]).
items.author: Tingting Liu, Dandan Song, Jun Chen et al.

However, little is known about how secondary school students in low-income settings perceive these environments and how such perceptions may influence their food practices. Methods A qualitative study was conducted in the municipalities of Natitingou (urban) and Boukombe (rural), Northern Benin, to explore secondary school students’ perceptions of their school food environments.

items.title: Variation in recommendations for management of pediatric fever and neutropenia across databases and languages: A systematic review of clinical practice guidelines
items.summary: by Asher Hancock, Brandon Fickling, Tea Reljic, Gabrielle M. Haeusler, Vivian Moreno Berrio, Ambuj Kumar, Sheena Mukkada Background Fever with neutropenia (FN) is a common complication of cancer therapy associated with significant morbidity, mortality, and resource use. Clinicians currently may access multiple Clinical Practice Guidelines (CPG) for FN in children to guide decision-making, however variation in content could impact care globally. We performed a systematic review and content analysis of CPG to assess the impact of databases searched and publication language on the quantity, quality, and content of recommendations identified for pediatric FN. Methods We conducted a systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science databases to identify evidence-based CPG published in the last 10 years addressing FN in children.
items.author: Asher Hancock, Brandon Fickling, Tea Reljic et al.

items.title: Approximate Synthetic Spectra of Quantum Systems Associated with Compact Lie Groups
items.summary: How can noncommuting quantum observables retain the geometry of a classical phase space? Motivated by Mumford's question on approximately macroscopically unique (AMU) states and the work of Lin and Wang, we study synthetic spectra of position--momentum and angular-momentum systems. Under the hypotheses of their AMU theorems, nonempty synthetic spectra yield AMU states. For sufficiently small $\hbar$, the position--momentum spectrum fills the plane, while the angular-momentum spectrum contains any prescribed ball. The latter calculation leads to compact Lie groups: we prove that highest-weight coadjoint orbits lie in regional synthetic spectra under an explicit variance bound. Function-space representations of $SU(n)$, $SO(n)$, and $Sp(n)$ provide further examples.
items.author: Junyang Liu, Hang Wang, Houjin Wang et al.

items.title: Comment on "Long-range magnetic fields in the ground state of the Standard Model plasma"
items.summary: We revisit the two-loop parity-odd photon polarization analyzed by Boyarsky, Ruchayskiy, and Shaposhnikov [Phys. Rev. Lett. 109, 111602 (2012)]. The original calculation neglected opposite- fermion-flow partner diagrams for the tadpole and exchange-bubble topologies alike. We quantify the impact of the properly restored exchange-bubble coefficients on the static magnetic response.
items.author: Jingwei Wang, Yiming Liu, Ligong Bian

items.title: An example of universal braiding in Links--Gould topological quantum computation
items.summary: We construct a universal quantum computational encoding via braiding in Links--Gould fusion spaces associated to $U_q^H(\mathfrak{sl}(2|1))$ where $q$ is on the unit circle and is not a root of unity. The construction uses only neglectons and is realized in the morphism spaces $\mathrm{Hom}_{U_q^H}(V(0,α),V(0,-\frac{1}{2})^{\otimes 2N}\otimes V(0,α)).$ Under explicit positivity and arithmetic constraints these spaces admit a $2^N$-dimensional computational subspace with a positive definite Hermitian form. We prove single-qubit density in $\mathrm{U}(2,1)$ and approximate arbitrary unitary operators on $N$-qubit computational subspaces with arbitrarily small leakage. The calculations use explicit inclusions, projections, and Hermitian pairings without requiring $F$-matrices.
items.author: Matthew Harper, Ben-Michael Kohli

items.title: Reasoning about Shared-Qubit Concurrency in Quantum Computing
items.summary: In this paper, we develop a semantic model for the parallel execution of quantum circuits, providing a formal foundation for studying shared-qubit concurrency in quantum computing. As in classical shared-memory concurrency, parallel quantum circuits may interfere with one another through operations on shared qubits. However, quantum entanglement and the noncommutativity of quantum operations introduce additional challenges for reasoning about their correctness. To address these challenges, we generalise the classical Owicki-Gries method to quantum computing at the level of quantum circuits. Our approach enables compositional reasoning about parallel quantum circuits by separating the verification of individual components from the analysis of interference between them.
items.author: Mingsheng Ying

items.title: Information-Geometric Representation of Upper Bounds on Fluctuation Growth in Open Quantum Systems
items.summary: Building on our earlier results for closed quantum systems, we investigate the dynamical evolution of quantum fluctuations and their connections to Fisher information and the quantum operations describing open-system dynamics. Starting from a general expression for the time derivative of an observable's uncertainty, we derive an alternative upper bound on fluctuation growth in an open quantum system using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality. The resulting bound separates contributions from the evolution of the quantum state and the explicit time dependence of the observable, reducing to a known result for closed-system dynamics. We then establish a connection between fluctuation dynamics and quantum Fisher information by decomposing the density operator and the symmetric logarithmic derivative (SLD) into coherent and incoherent contributions, which leads to a bound relating the evolution of observable uncertainty to the coherent and incoherent components of the Fisher information, providing an information-geometric interpretation of fluctuation growth.
items.author: Newshaw Bahreyni, Paul M. Alsing
